task: Built and deployed a complete same-session rate-limit auto-resume pipeline, fixed the root cause of quota-trigger failures (stale stats files), eliminated notification-button focus-steal UX antipattern, redesigned the guard escape-hatch to require explicit human approval instead of auto-passing, and added session-graph visualization and guard-block management CLI commands.
discussion_summary: The askr orchestrator now detects real quota exhaustion via independent live polling (bypassing stats-file staleness), sends Escape into the terminal to trigger the rate-limit reset menu, waits for the actual reset with premature-activity detection, and auto-resumes the session with 'cont' — all without requiring a new companion session. Notification buttons that run one-shot CLI commands (Keep/Discard, Approve/Discard, Add to Goals) now execute silently in the background instead of stealing focus by opening a new terminal. The guard's escape-hatch mechanism was redesigned from auto-allow-after-2-blocks (bypassable via retry alone) to held-for-approval (requires explicit `askr guard approve/discard` before proceeding). Handover generation now filters out hallucinated file paths, and next_actions staleness is prevented via corpus-overlap matching and git-commit cross-checks.

accomplishments.what: Implemented independent quota polling in lifecycle.py that fires the trigger even when stats files are stale (root cause of 90% trigger never firing)
Built five-stage same-session rate-limit auto-resume: detect via live poll → send Escape → target terminal via ancestor-PID → wait for reset with safety net → auto-send 'cont'
Redesigned guard escape-hatch from auto-allow-after-2-blocks to held-for-approval requiring explicit `askr guard approve/discard`
Converted all one-shot notification-button handlers (Keep/Discard, Approve/Discard, Add to Goals) to run silently via runAskrSilently() instead of creating visible terminals
Added `askr graph` CLI command rendering session-spawn tree from events.jsonl with trigger summaries
Added `askr guard list/approve/discard` CLI commands for managing guard blocks
Fixed handover hallucination by filtering files_in_play and relational_files against real filesystem before writing
Implemented next_actions staleness prevention via corpus-overlap matching (65% token threshold) and git-commit cross-checks
Extended mid-session CLAUDE.md reminder mechanism to combat context-decay adherence drift
Fixed test suite deadlock in test_turn_wait.py that was silently hanging entire pytest run
Added test isolation via conftest.py autouse fixture for hook_capture diagnostic logging
Committed and pushed all changes in stages with descriptive messages

decisions.decision: Use Escape key (\x1b) for quota-reset menu automation, not arrow-navigation or digit-selection
decisions.reason: Binary analysis proves Escape and manual 'Stop and wait' selection both call the same code path (der()); Escape is position-independent and sidesteps the risk of menu-order changes via remote feature flags

decisions.decision: Implement quota-reset automation in five stages: (1) instrumentation for detection, (2) PID→terminal bridge, (3) wait for real data, (4) wire automation, (5) safety-net detection
decisions.reason: Stages 1, 2, and 5 are buildable today without live events and carry no automation risk; Stage 3 requires real quota-limit data; Stage 4 (the only risky stage) waits for Stage 3 before proceeding

decisions.decision: PID→vscode.Terminal targeting uses _get_ancestor_pids to walk the process tree and findTerminalByAncestorPids to match Terminal by ancestor PID
decisions.reason: Claude Code may spawn multiple terminal instances; ancestor-PID matching is more reliable than terminal title or index-based targeting and survives terminal renames

decisions.decision: Guard escape-hatch holds writes for explicit human approval via `askr guard approve/discard` instead of auto-allowing after 2 blocks
decisions.reason: Auto-allow-after-retry-count was bypassable by simply retrying without genuine approach change; held-for-approval requires explicit human decision and prevents silent bypass

decisions.decision: Notification buttons for one-shot CLI commands (Keep/Discard, Approve/Discard, Add to Goals) run silently in background via runAskrSilently() instead of creating visible terminals
decisions.reason: User explicitly rejected the UX of new terminals stealing focus away from work; silent execution preserves user context while still running the command

decisions.decision: Filter hallucinated file paths from handover files_in_play and relational_files against real filesystem before writing
decisions.reason: Handover generation was inventing nonexistent files, wasting tokens on stale/invalid paths in next session; filesystem validation prevents this

decisions.decision: Prevent next_actions staleness via two mechanisms: corpus-overlap matching (65% token threshold) against git history + explicit git-commit cross-check
decisions.reason: Single mechanism was insufficient; combining both catches both token-level staleness and commit-level completion signals

user_rejected_decisions.what_was_proposed: Infer rate-limit exhaustion from session going quiet for an extended period
user_rejected_decisions.user_signal: no that really isn't any indication, and session having persistent gap can't be auto assumed to be rate-limited, we need the session exhausted limit recognition

user_rejected_decisions.what_was_proposed: Use a heuristic silence-based quota detection instead of independent live polling
user_rejected_decisions.user_signal: we need the session exhausted limit recognition, and we need to be able to press the stop and wait for limit to reset and the 'cont' message for the user, else we will not be able to achieve the overnight run

failed_approaches.approach: Using SIGTERM to kill Claude Code before in-flight compaction finishes
failed_approaches.reason: SIGTERM is treated as a graceful-shutdown signal; the target process honors it by finishing current work before exiting, allowing compaction to complete and generate the next response before the process actually dies

failed_approaches.approach: Using SIGTERM to kill Claude Code before compaction in pre_compact hook
failed_approaches.reason: Node.js catches SIGTERM and finishes the in-flight compaction + response before honoring the signal, defeating the race-prevention logic

failed_approaches.approach: Relying on passed-in session_id in _finish_emergency_checkpoint without fallback
failed_approaches.reason: session_id was empty by the time the function used it, causing every emergency companion_spawned event to log parent_session_id='', breaking session-tree reconstruction

failed_approaches.approach: Inferring rate-limit exhaustion from session inactivity gaps
failed_approaches.reason: Session gaps are not reliable indicators of rate-limit exhaustion; independent live polling via Anthropic's usage API is the only ground truth

failed_approaches.approach: Auto-allowing guard blocks after 2 retries without explicit human approval
failed_approaches.reason: Bypassable by simply retrying the same write without changing approach; user experienced this twice in real use, defeating the guard's safety purpose
